limitations: A four-wallet recursive DAG uses full-size circuits and fresh pair, merge and finalizer proofs through PoolCoordinator and LocalProcessEndpoint. Archived wallet inputs remain; no archived recursive proofs are imported.
Recovery occurs after clean worker and coordinator exits. This does not qualify crash recovery with live or unresolved physical workers, cancellation under load, multiple GPUs or remote workers.

The 600-second absolute workflow deadline survives all three phases. Each worker/coordinator/verifier service keeps its 180-second limit. This is not the full-64 or 180-second post-seal application gate.

Unmeasured warm estimates may use matching cold p95 plus the existing 10 percent margin, with measured=false. Exact warm observations take precedence. These observations are not deadline or performance guarantees.
These are proof and recovery qualification timings, not durably applied user transactions or matched delivered-throughput comparisons.
Observed resource limits and cleanup do not establish complete mapping, driver, kernel or scheduler phase-lifetime admission. Ordinary incomplete profiles remain inadmissible.

Broader live pool workloads and cache transitions, all maintained routes, matched delivered-throughput versus hybrid comparisons, 24 hours AND 150 roots, full-64/deadline/depth/size gates, multiple GPUs, AMD/Metal and pending Apple integration remain open.
